source_refs.title: Eureka Math / EngageNY, Grade 1, Module 5, Lesson 1

subject: math

objective.text: Sort shapes by their attributes, like how many straight sides and corners they have.

source_ref.section: Lesson objective

explanations.title: Open and closed shapes
explanations.text: A closed shape has no opening. Every end of every straw touches another straw. An open shape has an opening.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (Open Shapes / Closed Shapes)

explanations.title: What an attribute is
explanations.text: An attribute is a fact about a shape. 'Three straight sides' and 'three corners' are attributes.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (all of these shapes have two attributes)

explanations.title: Three sides and three corners
explanations.text: All the shapes on this chart share two attributes: three straight sides and three corners. A corner is where two sides meet.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (Chart 1: 3 Straight Sides and 3 Corners)

explanations.title: Four sides and four corners
explanations.text: These shapes look different, but all of them have four straight sides and four corners. Some corners are special square corners.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (Chart 2: 4 Corners and 4 Straight Sides)

explanations.title: Square corners
explanations.text: A square corner makes the same shape as the corner of a book. We can check a corner with a square corner tester.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (square corner tester)

examples.title: Record a straw shape
examples.text: Put your straw shape on paper. Draw a dot at every corner, where two straws meet. Move the straws away. Draw straight lines dot to dot.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (record the shape)

examples.title: Three straws, three sides, three corners
examples.text: This shape is made of 3 straws. It has 3 straight sides and 3 corners. Even when the sides have different lengths, it still has 3 sides and 3 corners.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (three-sided straw shape)

questions.text: Make both sides equal. 5 plus 5 equals 9 plus what number?

source_ref.section: Fluency: Make it Equal (worked example 5 + 5 = 9 + 1)

questions.text: Make both sides equal. 10 plus 0 equals 8 plus what number?

source_ref.section: Fluency: Make it Equal (suggested set 10, 8, 2, 0)

questions.text: You get 7 straw pieces. Your partner gets 7 straw pieces. You put them together. How many straw pieces can you use?

source_ref.section: Application Problem

questions.text: Look at this straw shape. How many straight sides does it have?

source_ref.section: Concept Development (S: three straight sides)

questions.text: Can you make a closed shape with four straight sides but only three corners? Answer yes or no.

source_ref.section: Student Debrief (four straight sides and only three corners)

questions.text: Two straws lie in a straight line, touching end to end. Are they one side or two sides?

source_ref.section: Student Debrief (two straws side by side can be one side)

questions.text: You join your straws with your partner's straws. You make a new shape with four straight sides and four corners. What must be true about your new shape?

misconceptions.label: Trouble seeing small differences between shapes
misconceptions.description: Some students find visual discrimination challenging, especially when the attributes are at more refined levels, such as counting sides and corners of similar shapes.
detection_signals: Counts a different number of sides or corners than the shape has.
Changes the answer when counting the same shape a second time.
misconceptions.response_text: Take your time. Touch each corner, or line up the straws, as you count.

source_ref.section: Notes on Multiple Means of Representation (visual discrimination)

assets_required.why_this_method: Side counts, corner counts and straw lengths must be exact, and pieces must snap together. Image models cannot count.
assets_required.description: Straw pieces of three lengths that snap end to end to build open and closed shapes, with tap-to-mark corner dots.
must_show_exactly: Straw pieces in exactly 3 lengths (full, half, quarter)
The shape for q_pr_1 has exactly 3 straight sides and 3 corners
Closed shapes have no gap; open shapes show a visible gap
Corner dots appear only where two straws meet
states_or_frames: Chart 2 shapes: 4 straight sides, 4 corners, varied lengths
corner dots placed at each join
assets_required.interaction: Child drags straw pieces; pieces snap end to end. Tap a join to mark a corner dot. Tutor can load a fixed shape from the question stimulus.
assets_required.alt_text: Straw pieces joined end to end to make a shape.
assets_required.generation_caption: Flat colourful straw pieces in three lengths on a plain desk background, child-friendly style. [Build by code]

assets_required.why_this_method: The L-shaped tester must fit corners exactly; the fit check is behaviour, not a picture.
assets_required.description: An L-shaped square corner tester the child drags onto each corner of a shape to check whether it is a square corner.
must_show_exactly: The tester is a true right angle (L shape)
It fits exactly only into square corners
states_or_frames: tester placed into a corner: fits (square corner)
tester placed into a corner: does not fit (not a square corner)
assets_required.interaction: Drag the tester onto a corner. It glows green when it fits and red when it does not.
assets_required.alt_text: An L-shaped tool checking the corner of a shape.
assets_required.generation_caption: Simple bright L-shaped corner tool, flat style, plain background. [Build by code]

Source is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (Great Minds). Cards must credit Great Minds, stay non-commercial, and be shared under the same license. The word license must stay in the card.

review_flags.item: Problem Set items 1-8, Exit Ticket 1-2, Homework 1-8, square-corner counting
review_flags.issue: These items are picture-only (circle, draw, and count from shape pictures). The uploaded DOCX is text-only with no images attached, so the shapes cannot be read. Not added as questions. Needs human or vision extraction from the original PDF pages.
Image models cannot be trusted for counts. Use code-rendered visuals for anything with exact numbers, and have a person check each visual against the answer key.
Both assets (a_straw_shapes, a_square_corner_tester) are not_available. Items that use them cannot launch until the asset exists.
All child-facing text was rewritten from a 60-minute teacher script with classroom objects into screen wording. Needs an age-appropriate wording review.
ext_k_basic_shapes is an external prerequisite (ext_) that has no card yet. The lesson assumes Kindergarten knowledge of open and closed shapes.

Sprint A items used: 1, 2, 3, 6, 8, 10, 11, 18, 28, 30 (every distinct pattern once: +1, +2, +3, adding to 5, missing addend in three positions, balanced equations both ways). Sprint B adds no new pattern, so no B items were used. Remaining items are parallel repeats of used patterns.
Single-number answers have no sensible partial outcome. The script must map partial to the same path as incorrect, or the schema must allow null.
The source states only one misconception and few hint moves, and all explanations come from one straw-building activity. Hint coverage is thin and the Planner has little real choice. Needs review.
The Sprint pages and the Application Problem have no printed answers. All Sprint answers and the application answer (14) are derived and were recomputed twice.
Only 1.OA.6 and 1.OA.7 are printed in this lesson file. The focus standard 1.G.1 appears in the Topic Overview, not in the lesson text, so it was not added.
The text-only DOCX has no page footer, so 'This file derived from...' could not be read. source_version is a placeholder; confirm it against the original PDF footer.

visual_generation_rules: Diffusion cannot count reliably. Any picture where an exact number of objects matters must be built by code (SVG or widget) or drawn by an artist.
Diffusion is allowed only for: style or background art, and single icons (one ball, one pencil, one leaf, one character) that code then tiles to the exact count.
Every visual must be checked by a person: the count shown must equal the stimulus in the question and the rubric answer key.
Animations are described as frames with exact counts per frame, so they can be built or generated and then checked frame by frame.
Visual explanations are valid only when the asset exists (pipeline doc, Planner rules).
